function: Learned design of 1-bit RIS phase shifts (BeamNet) and time-frequency resource-block allocation (AllocationNet) to maximize sum rate; BS beamforming is MRT with water-filling, not learned. pp. 1, 4
system: BS with 4 antennas, 3 single-antenna users, passive reflecting RIS with 64 1-bit elements, OFDMA with 16 subcarriers of 180 kHz; carrier band not stated. pp. 4, 7
method: Unsupervised learning: two CNN-based networks with squeeze-and-excitation residual block, Gumbel-softmax and quantization layer, custom sum-rate loss with QoS penalty, five-stage phased training from scratch. pp. 4-7
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rayleigh direct link, Rician multi-tap BS-RIS and RIS-user links, power-law path loss; 4,900 training and 100 validation samples, results averaged over 100 realizations. pp. 7-8
test_conditions: Trained with delay taps 4/2/3, user radius 10 m, Rician factors 2/4 dB; tested with taps 6/3/4, radius 15 m, and other Rician factors. pp. 10-11
baselines: Non-learned: continuous SCA [37], discrete (quantized) SCA, random RB allocation, random RIS, no RIS; no earlier learned method compared. p. 8
metrics: Sum rate, 5th-percentile user rate versus the QoS threshold, runtime, percentage of SCA performance, training and validation loss. pp. 8-9, 12
complexity: BeamNet O(K^2NtNM+QM), AllocationNet O(Q^2NtNK+QNK), beamforming O(QNMNt+QN); runtime 18.35 ms versus 49642.81 ms for discrete SCA at M=64. p. 12
q1_support: p. 7: "Rayleigh fading channels are assumed, while Rician fading is considered for the reflection channels". Custom simulator with its own path-loss exponents (p. 8); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 10: "the delay tap numbers in the testing environment are set to L0 = 6, L1 = 3, and L2 = 4, while the network is trained using datasets with delay tap numbers L0 = 4, L1 = 2, and L2 = 3". Also tested at another user radius (p. 11) and Rician factors (p. 11).
q3_support: p. 8: "Continuous SCA: The algorithm proposed in [37] is employed for RB allocation and RIS reflection phase shift optimization" is the non-learned baseline. The other comparisons are random allocation, random RIS, no RIS and variants of the proposed method; no earlier learned method or standard network is compared.
q4_support: p. 12: "Table III reports the runtime and performance of each algorithm"; the same page gives the O() complexity of BeamNet, AllocationNet and beamforming, and a runtime of 18.35 ms at M = 64.
q5_support: p. 8: "4,900 and 100 data samples were generated as the training and validation sets". Data are self-simulated; no code or data link and no public dataset is given.
notes: Included. The learned BeamNet sets the RIS phase shifts (an area 3 function), so the joint learning with RB allocation passes the above_phy check. Main metric is sum rate, so area 3. Table II and Table III were read from the page images (pp. 8, 12).
